questions.stem: In Colorado, when does a single agency relationship, such as buyer agency, exist?
choices: Once the broker has shown the buyer a property
When the buyer orally asks the broker to represent him
Only under a written agreement signed before brokerage activities
When the seller accepts an offer the broker wrote for the buyer
questions.explanation: Single agency requires a written agreement with the represented party, signed before the broker begins brokerage activities for that party. Without one, the broker is presumed to be a transaction-broker.

questions.stem: A Colorado seller's agent wants other MLS brokers to act as subagents of her seller. Which statement is correct?
choices: It's allowed as long as the seller consents to it in writing
Not allowed; she may cooperate with them but not create subagents
It's allowed only for brokers who work in the same firm
It's required for every listing entered in the MLS
questions.explanation: A Colorado single agent may cooperate with other brokers but may not engage or create subagents. Old-style MLS subagency is not available in Colorado, even with the seller's consent.

questions.stem: A seller's agent is about to work with an unrepresented buyer. Before engaging in brokerage activities with the buyer, the broker's written disclosure must state that:
choices: the buyer will be vicariously liable for the broker's acts
the broker will keep the buyer's price limit confidential
the broker will act as a transaction-broker for the buyer
the broker is the seller's agent and not the buyer's agent
questions.explanation: A seller's agent working with a buyer must disclose in writing that the broker is the seller's agent and not the buyer's, list the tasks the broker will do for the seller, and state that the buyer is not vicariously liable for the agent's acts.

questions.stem: A buyer refuses to sign the acknowledgment on a Brokerage Disclosure to Buyer form. What should the broker do?
choices: Stop working with the buyer, since the form is a required contract
Note the refusal and date on a copy and keep that copy
Ask the employing broker to sign the form on the buyer's behalf
Send the unsigned form to the Division within 3 business days
questions.explanation: The acknowledgment is a receipt, not a contract, so the buyer's refusal doesn't end the relationship. The broker records the refusal and the date on a copy and keeps it (with the delivery email if sent electronically).

questions.stem: A firm's written office policy offers only transaction-brokerage. A buyer asks the broker about buyer agency. What must the broker do?
choices: Give the buyer the Commission's written definition of buyer agency
Refer the buyer to the Division of Real Estate for an explanation
Nothing, because the firm doesn't offer buyer agency
Act as the buyer's agent anyway, since the buyer requested it in person
questions.explanation: A firm need not offer every relationship, but if a party asks about one the firm doesn't offer, the broker must provide the Commission's written definition of it, which is what the Definitions of Working Relationships form is for.

questions.stem: Three brokers at one firm work as a team on a seller's listing. Which statement is correct?
choices: Only the team leader must be designated; others may assist as needed
Members may serve the seller in different capacities if the seller agrees
Every member must be designated in the same capacity and named in the listing
Using a team makes the entire firm the seller's agent for the listing
questions.explanation: Commission rules require every team member to be a designated broker for the consumer in the same capacity, and all members must be named in the listing contract. Designation never extends the relationship to the whole firm.

questions.stem: Which statement about a Colorado employing broker in a firm that uses designated brokerage is correct?
choices: Designating brokers ends the employing broker's duty to supervise them
The firm needs a written policy on which relationships it offers
Clients become vicariously liable for acts of the brokers they hire
The employing broker may never be the designated broker in a transaction
questions.explanation: The employing broker must adopt a written office policy describing the relationships offered, how brokers are designated and how confidential information is protected. Designation doesn't reduce the duty to supervise, and the employing broker may be a designated broker.

questions.stem: Under Colorado's brokerage relationships statute, a relationship that is not completed ends at the earliest of the agreed expiration date, termination by the parties, or:
choices: 90 days after it began
two years after it began
the end of the broker's license period
one year after it began
questions.explanation: If the engagement isn't completed, the relationship ends at the earliest of its expiration date, termination by the parties, or one year after it began.

questions.stem: A seller's property is under contract. Her listing broker, a seller's agent, receives another written offer. What must the broker do?
choices: Hold it until the current contract terminates
Present it to the seller in a timely manner
Return it, since property under contract can't receive offers
Present it only if it beats the current contract price
questions.explanation: A single agent must present all offers to and from the client in a timely manner, even when the property is already under contract. What the agent need not do is go looking for more offers while it's under contract.

questions.stem: A buyer's agent's client is about to make an offer on a home. Another of the agent's buyer clients wants to make an offer on the same home. Under Colorado law, the agent:
choices: may help both buyers try to buy it without breaching a duty
must drop one buyer, since helping both breaches loyalty
must become a transaction-broker for both buyers
needs the seller's written consent to help the second buyer
questions.explanation: Colorado's statute says a buyer's agent may show the same property to competing buyers and help them try to buy it; this is not a breach of duty to the first buyer.

questions.stem: A seller pays the fee of a broker who worked with the buyer. Does the payment make the broker the seller's agent?
choices: Yes, a broker is always the agent of the party who pays
Yes, unless the buyer signed a written agreement first
No; payment alone doesn't create an agency relationship
No, because only buyers may pay a buyer's broker in Colorado
questions.explanation: Colorado separates who pays from who is represented: compensation may come from either party or a third party, and paying a broker does not, by itself, create agency.

questions.stem: A homeowner wants a broker to start marketing her home but refuses to sign any listing contract. What is the broker's position?
choices: The broker may market it as a transaction-broker without a listing
The broker may proceed on an oral listing if a witness is present
The broker may proceed after giving her a Brokerage Disclosure form
The broker may not perform brokerage services for her
questions.explanation: A seller or landlord listing must be in writing before any brokerage services are performed, whatever the relationship. If the seller refuses to sign, the broker can't provide brokerage services to her.

questions.stem: Under the Exclusive Right-to-Buy contract, the buyer's brokerage is paid partly from the seller's side and the buyer owes the rest. When does the buyer owe an unpaid balance?
choices: Only if disclosed in writing before the buyer signs the purchase contract
Whenever the seller side pays less, regardless of when it was disclosed
Only if the seller's agent agrees in writing to the buyer paying it
Only if the closing company approves the amount at closing
questions.explanation: Under the 2026 Exclusive Right-to-Buy form, the buyer owes the portion of the fee the seller side doesn't pay only if the broker disclosed the amount to the buyer in writing before the buyer entered into a contract with the seller. Neither the seller's agent nor the closing company can create that obligation.

questions.stem: A residential buyer is offered an engagement contract that would record a lien against her future home to secure the broker's fee. Under C.R.S. 12-10-403.5:
choices: the lien is valid once the contract is recorded with the county
the lien is valid only if the buyer initials that paragraph
the lien is void only if the contract runs longer than one year
it's void, and offering it is a deceptive trade practice
questions.explanation: A residential engagement contract may not create a lien, encumbrance or other recordable interest in the property; any such interest is void, and offering a contract with that term is a deceptive trade practice.

questions.stem: A broker wants to put earnest money in a 12-month certificate of deposit at the trust account bank. Without a written agreement of the parties, this is:
choices: allowed if the CD is titled in the firm's name as a trust account
allowed as long as the broker agrees to pay any withdrawal penalty
not allowed; trust funds must be available at once without penalty
allowed only for earnest money held longer than 30 days
questions.explanation: Trust funds must be available immediately without penalty, so CDs and other fixed-term investments aren't allowed unless the parties agree otherwise in writing.

questions.stem: A Colorado sales firm never holds earnest money because title companies always hold it. How many trust accounts must it maintain?
choices: None; a firm that holds no one else's money may have zero
At least one, titled as a sales escrow account
Two: one for earnest money and one for security deposits
One for each associate broker in the firm
questions.explanation: A firm may have any number of trust accounts, including zero, if it never receives money belonging to others.

questions.stem: A firm's trust account earns interest, and no written agreement says who gets it. Under the Commission's position, the interest:
choices: belongs to the firm as the account holder
is split equally between the firm and the beneficiaries
doesn't belong to the brokerage firm
must be sent to the State Treasurer every month
questions.explanation: Absent a specific written agreement, interest on a trust account does not belong to the firm; keeping it would be undisclosed compensation. The contract, management agreement or lease should say who gets it.

questions.stem: A seller accepts a buyer's promissory note as earnest money. The note isn't paid when due. What must the broker do?
choices: Promptly tell the seller and give the seller the original note
Keep the note in the firm's file and wait for the closing date
Cancel the contract for the seller and return the note to the buyer
Cover the amount with firm funds and collect from the buyer later
questions.explanation: When a note is accepted as earnest money, the seller must be told when it's due; if it isn't paid then, the broker must promptly notify the seller and deliver the original note to the seller.

questions.stem: After a contract terminates, the buyer authorizes in writing that the earnest money go to the seller. The holding brokerage:
choices: must first get the seller's signature on a release as well
may require both parties to sign a release holding the firm harmless
should disburse it as directed without unnecessary delay
must wait for a court order before releasing the money
questions.explanation: When the parties agree, the holder disburses as directed without delay; one party's written authorization in favor of the other is enough. The firm may not demand a hold-harmless or liability-waiver release.

questions.stem: Which deposit of a firm's own money into its trust account is permitted?
choices: A standing cushion of firm money so trust checks never bounce
Earned commissions left in the account until year-end
The employing broker's personal savings, to shield them from creditors
Funds to cover the account's bank charges, recorded in the records
questions.explanation: A firm may deposit its own money to cover bank charges (or a recorded, labeled advance for a client). A cushion, or earned fees left in the account, is commingling; earned fees must be withdrawn monthly.

questions.stem: Management of a rental property moves from Firm A to Firm B. Which deadlines apply to the tenants' security deposits?
choices: B discloses their status within 10 days; A transfers them within 30 days
B discloses their status within 30 days; A transfers them within 60 days
A transfers them within 5 business days; no written disclosure is needed
A refunds the tenants, who then pay new deposits to Firm B
questions.explanation: Commission rules give the new firm 30 days after the management agreement is signed or assigned to disclose the deposits' status in writing to the owner and tenant, and the prior firm 60 days to transfer the deposits to the new firm. Refunding and re-collecting deposits isn't the procedure.

questions.stem: A property management agreement says nothing about owner reports. When are reports to the owner due?
choices: Within 30 days after the end of the month funds were received or paid
Within 10 business days after each tenant's rent payment arrives
Once a year, by January 31 for the prior calendar year
Only when the owner asks for a report in writing
questions.explanation: Reports follow the management agreement; if it's silent, Commission rules require them within 30 days after the end of the month in which funds were received or disbursed. The other timeframes aren't in the rules.

questions.stem: Which item is part of the trust account records a Colorado firm must keep?
choices: A copy of each party's credit report and tax return
Annual financial statements audited by an outside CPA firm
A monthly balance report filed with the Division of Real Estate
Written accounting control policies for people who handle money
questions.explanation: Required trust records include the journal, beneficiary ledgers, monthly three-way reconciliations, bank statements, signed deposit agreements, and written accounting control policies describing checks and balances over people who handle money.

questions.stem: Which written office policy must a Colorado employing broker have concerning records?
choices: A policy for disposing of documents with personal identifying info
A policy requiring all emails and texts to be kept for ten years
A policy for filing every transaction file with the Commission at closing
A policy requiring paper copies of all electronic records
questions.explanation: The employing broker's office policies must include a written policy for disposing of documents containing personal identifying information. Keeping emails and texts is recommended, not required, and electronic records are allowed.

questions.stem: In a Colorado disciplinary matter, which statement correctly describes the roles?
choices: The Commission investigates and the Division decides the discipline
The Division investigates and the Commission decides the discipline
The Attorney General's office both investigates and decides
Local REALTOR boards investigate and the Division decides
questions.explanation: The Division of Real Estate investigates; the Colorado Real Estate Commission decides whether a violation occurred and what discipline fits.

questions.stem: A broker who settled a disciplinary case agreed to follow-up audits of her firm. How was the firm selected for these audits?
choices: At random
By MLS referral
At license renewal
By stipulation
questions.explanation: The Division selects firms for audit randomly, by stipulation (a settlement in which the broker agrees to follow-up audits), or as a result of a complaint or investigation.

questions.stem: A seller files a complaint asking the Division to interpret a contract clause in her favor and make the buyer's broker repay her losses. What is the likely result?
choices: The Commission orders the broker to reimburse her for the losses
The Division interprets the contract clause and then enforces it
Dismissal; contract disputes and money claims are civil matters
The complaint goes to an administrative law judge for a ruling
questions.explanation: Staff first check jurisdiction. Interpreting or enforcing a contract is a civil matter for an attorney or the courts, and Commission discipline isn't a way to collect money from a broker.

questions.stem: Which of these is a public record?
choices: A pending complaint filed against a broker with the Division
The investigator's file on an open investigation
A stipulation settling a disciplinary case
The name of a complainant who filed anonymously
questions.explanation: Complaints and investigation files are closed to the public. Stipulations and final agency orders are public records.

questions.stem: A disciplinary case against a broker does not settle. Who conducts the hearing?
choices: The full Real Estate Commission
The Division director
A district court jury
An administrative law judge
questions.explanation: An administrative law judge from the Office of Administrative Courts hears the case under the state Administrative Procedure Act; the Commission then decides by majority vote, and the Court of Appeals reviews.

questions.stem: Broker A, a designated seller's agent, knows his seller would accept $15,000 less. Broker B, at the same firm, is the designated buyer's agent for a buyer interested in the home. Which is correct?
choices: B is presumed to know it, since both brokers work for the same firm
A can't reveal it without the seller's consent; B isn't charged with knowing it
A must tell B, because the employing broker is now a dual agent
A must disclose it, since the price is an adverse material fact
questions.explanation: A seller's agent may not disclose that the seller would accept less without the seller's informed consent. With designated brokerage, A's knowledge isn't imputed to B, and two designated agents on opposite sides isn't dual agency.

questions.stem: A firm holds the earnest money on a sale that closes. Which trust records must it keep, and for how long?
choices: Only the bank statements, for 3 years after the deposit
Journal and ledgers only, for 5 years from opening the file
Only the closing statement, for 4 years from the listing date
Journal, ledgers and reconciliations, for 4 years from closing
questions.explanation: Each trust account needs a journal, beneficiary ledgers and monthly three-way reconciliation reports, and required records are kept four years from closing (or from listing expiration if it never closed).

questions.stem: A broker has no written agreement with a buyer and has given the transaction-broker disclosure. The buyer says she'd pay $10,000 more than her offer. May the broker tell the seller?
choices: Yes, since a transaction-broker is not the buyer's agent
Yes, as long as the seller asks the broker about it directly
Not without the informed consent of all parties
No, because without a written agreement the broker is the buyer's agent
questions.explanation: Without a written single-agency agreement the broker is a presumed transaction-broker, and a transaction-broker may not disclose that a buyer would pay more without the informed consent of all parties.
